stem: Best guess: a trust distributes all of its interest income to its beneficiary. Who pays the tax on that income?

choices.explanation: The income is taxed once, to the beneficiary.
Correct. The distribution deduction shifts the tax to the beneficiary.

explanation: The distribution deduction shifts the tax to the beneficiary.

stem: In computing DNI for a trust that allocates capital gains to corpus and doesn't distribute them, capital gains are:

choices.explanation: Gains allocated to corpus are excluded from DNI.
Correct. §643(a)(3): gains allocated to corpus and not distributed are excluded from DNI and taxed to the trust.

explanation: §643(a)(3): gains allocated to corpus and not distributed are excluded from DNI and taxed to the trust.

stem: What does the 65-day election allow?

choices.text: Distributions within 65 days to count for the prior year
choices.explanation: Correct. §663(b) lets the trustee manage DNI after year-end.

choices.text: A trust to choose a fiscal year
choices.explanation: Only estates may choose a fiscal year.

choices.text: An extension of time to file Form 1041
Grantor trust treatment for the year
choices.explanation: Grantor status depends on retained powers.

explanation: §663(b) lets the trustee manage DNI after year-end.

stem: What is the personal exemption for a complex trust?

choices.explanation: Correct. §642(b): estates $600; simple trusts $300; other trusts $100.

explanation: §642(b): estates $600; simple trusts $300; other trusts $100.

stem: A simple trust has taxable interest of $20,000 and trustee fees of $2,000 allocated to income. It distributes accounting income of $18,000. What is the trust's taxable income?

choices.explanation: Correct. 18,000 − 18,000 deduction; the $300 exemption can't create a loss.

explanation: Income 20,000 − fees 2,000 = 18,000 = DNI = distribution deduction.

stem: For 2025 the 37% trust rate applies to taxable income over $15,650. A trust has 2025 taxable income of $20,000 (all ordinary). Which rate applies to its last dollar of income?

choices.explanation: The 37% bracket begins at $15,650 for trusts.
Correct. Trusts reach the top bracket at $15,650 (2025).

explanation: Trusts reach the top bracket at $15,650 (2025).

stem: A complex trust has DNI of $40,000, including $8,000 of net tax-exempt interest. It distributes $40,000. What is the distribution deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. §661(c): no deduction for the tax-exempt portion of the distribution.
The exemption isn't part of the distribution deduction.

explanation: §661(c): no deduction for the tax-exempt portion of the distribution.

stem: Which trust's income is taxed to the grantor?

choices.text: An irrevocable trust in which the grantor retained no powers
choices.explanation: Taxed to the trust or beneficiaries.

choices.text: A testamentary trust created by a will

choices.explanation: Correct. A revocable trust is a grantor trust (§676).

explanation: A revocable trust is a grantor trust (§676).

stem: When is Form 1041 due for a calendar-year 2025 trust, without extension?

choices.explanation: Correct. 15th day of the 4th month after year-end.

explanation: 15th day of the 4th month after year-end.

stem: An estate's executor is choosing a tax year. What planning opportunity is available to estates but not most trusts?

choices.text: A fiscal year to defer beneficiaries' income
choices.explanation: Correct. §644 requires trusts to use a calendar year; estates may choose a fiscal year.

choices.text: No filing requirement in the first year
choices.explanation: Estates file Form 1041 at $600 of gross income.

explanation: §644 requires trusts to use a calendar year; estates may choose a fiscal year.

stem: A trust's beneficiary is in the 12% bracket; the trust will have $30,000 of undistributed interest taxed at up to 37%. The trustee has discretion to distribute. What is the most tax-efficient action?

choices.text: Accumulate the income in the trust for later
Distribute it, possibly within 65 days after year-end
choices.explanation: Correct. Distribution shifts income to the beneficiary's lower bracket.

choices.text: Reclassify the income as trust corpus
Invest in growth stocks next year instead

explanation: Distribution shifts income to the beneficiary's lower bracket.

stem: A trust's gross income is $500 and it has no taxable income. Must it file Form 1041?

choices.text: Yes, because all trusts must file every year
No, unless a beneficiary is a nonresident alien
choices.explanation: Correct. Form 1041 is required with gross income of $600 or more, any taxable income, or a nonresident alien beneficiary.

choices.text: Yes, because it had some gross income
choices.explanation: The threshold is $600 of gross income.

choices.text: Only if it made distributions during the year

explanation: Form 1041 is required with gross income of $600 or more, any taxable income, or a nonresident alien beneficiary.

stem: Trust DNI is $30,000: $18,000 of interest and $12,000 of qualified dividends. It distributes $15,000 to a single beneficiary. What does the beneficiary report?

choices.explanation: Distributions carry the character of DNI proportionately.
Correct. Each class of income is distributed proportionately: 60% interest, 40% dividends.

explanation: Each class of income is distributed proportionately: 60% interest, 40% dividends.

stem: Which trust is a simple trust for the year?

choices.text: One that must distribute all income
choices.explanation: Correct. And makes no charity or principal payments.

choices.text: One that pays principal to beneficiaries

explanation: A simple trust must distribute all income currently, makes no charitable contributions and distributes no principal.

stem: What personal exemption does an estate get on Form 1041?
explanation: Estates have a $600 exemption; simple trusts $300; complex trusts $100.

stem: A complex trust distributes $10,000 on February 20, 2026. How can the trustee treat it as a 2025 distribution?

choices.text: It can't be done after year-end

choices.explanation: Correct. Distributions within 65 days can count for the prior year.

explanation: §663(b): distributions within 65 days after year-end may be treated as paid in the prior year by election.

stem: After an employee dies, her employer pays her final $8,000 salary to her son. How does he treat it?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income in respect of a decedent.

explanation: Income in respect of a decedent is taxed to the recipient with the same character; it gets no basis step-up.

stem: A simple trust has $10,000 of interest, distributed, and a $20,000 capital gain allocated to corpus. What is the trust's taxable income?

choices.explanation: Corpus gains are taxed to the trust.

explanation: Capital gains allocated to corpus are excluded from DNI and taxed to the trust: $20,000 − $300 = $19,700.

stem: A grantor sells assets to an intentionally defective grantor trust. How is the trust treated?

choices.explanation: Correct. Outside the estate but taxed to the grantor.

explanation: An IDGT is a grantor trust for income tax, but transfers to it are completed gifts outside the grantor's estate.

stem: A decedent leaves $5,000,000 outright to his U.S.-citizen wife. What estate tax deduction applies?

choices.explanation: Correct. It's unlimited for citizen spouses.

explanation: The estate tax marital deduction is unlimited for qualifying transfers to a U.S.-citizen spouse.

stem: When is Form 706 due, without extension?

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.
That isn't what the rule says.

explanation: The estate tax return is due 9 months after the date of death.

stem: In its final year, a trust's deductions exceed its gross income. What happens to the excess?

choices.text: It's lost when the trust ends

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.

explanation: On termination, excess deductions and unused carryovers pass to the beneficiaries succeeding to the property.

stem: A trust has undistributed investment income above the top-bracket threshold. What extra tax may apply?

choices.explanation: Correct. Trusts reach it at low income.

explanation: Trusts owe NIIT on the lesser of undistributed NII or AGI above the threshold for the top trust bracket.

stem: An estate executor can choose any tax year-end. Why might she choose a fiscal year ending January 31?

choices.text: Estates must use a fiscal year

choices.explanation: Correct. Distributions are taxed in the beneficiary year that includes the estate's year-end.

choices.text: To lower the estate tax owed

explanation: Estates may adopt a fiscal year, deferring beneficiaries' inclusion of distributions.

stem: A beneficiary receives $100,000 of IRD included in the decedent's estate; $40,000 of estate tax is attributable to it. How is it taxed?

choices.text: No income, due to a step-up

choices.explanation: Correct. The deduction relieves double taxation.

explanation: IRD is income to the recipient, who deducts estate tax attributable to it.

stem: A complex trust has DNI of $50,000. It must distribute $40,000 of income to A (tier 1) and makes a $30,000 discretionary distribution to B (tier 2). How much is taxable to B?

choices.explanation: DNI is used by tier 1 first.
Correct. Tier 1 absorbs $40,000 of DNI first.

explanation: Under the tier system, required income distributions absorb DNI before discretionary distributions.

stem: When is Form 1041 due for a calendar-year trust?

choices.explanation: Correct. The 15th day of the 4th month.

explanation: Form 1041 is due on the 15th day of the 4th month after the tax year ends.

stem: What personal exemption does a simple trust get?
explanation: Simple trusts get $300, complex trusts $100 and estates $600.

stem: For 2025, at what taxable income does a trust reach the 37% bracket?
explanation: Trusts reach the top bracket at very low income: $15,650 in 2025.

stem: A trust has $20,000 of taxable interest, $5,000 of tax-exempt interest, $10,000 of capital gains allocated to corpus and $3,000 of fees. What is DNI?
explanation: DNI includes tax-exempt income and excludes capital gains allocated to corpus.

stem: A simple trust has $30,000 of taxable interest and no other items. It distributes all income as required. What is the trust's tax result?
explanation: A simple trust deducts required income distributions up to DNI.

stem: A complex trust has $40,000 of DNI (all taxable) and distributes $25,000. What is the trust's taxable income?
explanation: The trust is taxed on undistributed income less its exemption.

stem: A trust distributes $50,000 to a beneficiary, and its DNI is $40,000. How much does the beneficiary include?
explanation: Beneficiaries include distributions in income up to DNI.

stem: DNI of $40,000 consists of $30,000 of interest and $10,000 of qualified dividends, all distributed. How does the beneficiary report it?
explanation: Distributions keep the character of the trust's income.

stem: A trustee distributes income on February 20 of the following year. What election lets it count for the prior year?

choices.explanation: Correct. For complex trusts and estates.

explanation: §663(b) lets distributions within 65 days after year-end be treated as made in the prior year.

stem: A complex trust realizes a $20,000 capital gain allocated to corpus. Who generally pays tax on it?

choices.explanation: Correct. Corpus gains stay in the trust.

explanation: Capital gains allocated to corpus are generally excluded from DNI and taxed to the trust.

stem: A trust's grantor keeps the power to revoke it. Who is taxed on its income?
explanation: Income of a grantor trust is taxed to the grantor.

stem: What does a §645 election do?

choices.text: Makes the trust a grantor trust
Joins the trust to the estate
choices.explanation: Correct. It allows estate tax-year and other benefits.

explanation: §645 lets a qualified revocable trust be treated as part of the estate for income tax.

stem: A trust has $50,000 of undistributed net investment income and $50,000 of AGI in 2025. What NIIT applies?
explanation: Trusts owe NIIT on the lesser of undistributed NII or AGI above the top bracket threshold.

stem: A 2025 estate is worth $20,000,000, with a $3,000,000 marital deduction and no prior taxable gifts. The exclusion is $13,990,000. What estate tax is due?
explanation: Estate tax is 40% of the taxable estate above the exclusion.

stem: In its final year, a trust has deductions exceeding its income. What happens to the excess?

choices.explanation: It passes out in this case.

choices.text: It carries forward in the trust

explanation: Excess deductions on termination pass to the beneficiaries succeeding to the property.

stem: A trust is in the 37% bracket, and its beneficiaries are in the 12% bracket. What should the trustee consider?

choices.explanation: Not a plan in this case.
Correct. It shifts income to lower brackets.

explanation: Distributions carry DNI to lower-bracket beneficiaries.

stem: After year-end, a trustee sees the trust owes tax at 37% on accumulated income. What can still reduce it?

choices.explanation: Correct. Elected for the prior year.

explanation: A 65-day distribution and election shifts income to beneficiaries for the prior year.

stem: A grantor wants to remove appreciation from her estate while paying the trust's income tax herself. What structure fits?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income tax stays with the grantor.

explanation: An IDGT is outside the estate for estate tax but taxed to the grantor, who pays the trust's tax.

stem: An estate's executor is choosing its first tax year. What flexibility does the estate have?

choices.explanation: Correct. Estates may choose a fiscal year.

explanation: Estates may adopt any fiscal year ending within 12 months of death, which can defer income.

stem: A trust has large undistributed investment income. How can NIIT be reduced?

choices.text: Convert it to a C corporation

explanation: Individuals' NIIT thresholds are much higher than the trust threshold.

stem: A surviving spouse wants her late husband's unused exclusion. What must the executor do?
explanation: Portability of the DSUE amount requires an election on a timely filed estate tax return.
